paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: Paul says there is no authority except that which is from God (Romans 13:1). That's why he tells everyone to submit to the governing authorities. It's not because rulers are always right or always know best. It's because God is the One who has set them in place.

Then Paul gives the baker two reasons to live this way. One is to avoid punishment, because the one in authority "does not carry the sword in vain" (Romans 13:4). The other is "as a matter of conscience" (Romans 13:5). So this isn't about tiptoeing around the boss with your shoulders up by your ears. It's about doing what's right because you know who is behind the whole arrangement.

And Paul brings it all the way down to everyday life. Pay taxes, because the authorities are God's servants, who devote themselves to their work (Romans 13:6). Then pay "respect to whom respect is due, honor to whom honor is due" (Romans 13:7). That bill never stops coming, baker, and I'm still working on mine, but we can pay it with good conduct and a clear conscience, knowing God is the One we answer to in the end.
